diagnosis.summary: All three services are experiencing a roughly 3x traffic spike that began at 14:03 UTC. Request rates rose from 15 to 45.1 rps on product-service, 2 to 6 rps on cart-service, and 2.9 to 8.8 rps on order-service. Latencies and error rates remain largely nominal across all services.
diagnosis.root_cause: A sudden surge in inbound traffic across all three services is the most likely root cause, consistent with an external traffic spike such as a flash sale, bot activity, or marketing campaign driving concurrent load.
evidence: Product-service request rate rose from 15 to 45.1 rps, a 3x increase
Cart-service request rate rose from 2 to 6 rps, a 3x increase
Order-service request rate rose from 2.9 to 8.8 rps, roughly a 3x increase
Product-service p95 latency increased modestly from 24 ms to 31 ms (29% rise), well within normal range
Order-service p95 latency increased slightly from 58 ms to 61 ms (5% rise), remaining healthy
Product-service 5xx error rate is 0%, indicating no failures despite the traffic surge
recommended_actions: Monitor Lambda concurrent executions and DynamoDB consumed capacity across all three services to detect any approaching limits before throttling begins
Review API Gateway throttling and Lambda reserved concurrency settings to ensure headroom if traffic continues to climb
Investigate the traffic source (CloudFront or API Gateway access logs) to determine whether the spike is legitimate user traffic or bot activity
If the spike is expected to persist or grow, consider enabling DynamoDB auto-scaling or switching to on-demand capacity mode on all three tables
